text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At least 34,000 secondary school teachers receive pay rises of between 10 and 46 percent.
- The government acts to stall a strike by air traffic controllers by assuring them it will not renege on its promise to improve their terms of service.
- The U.N. Development Programme recommends upgrading Nairobi to a metropolitan city status.
- Riotous demonstrations in Nairobi's streets continue as members of the public express grief over the mysterious death of student leader Solomon Muruli.
- A post-mortem examination on the late Muruli is delayed.
- Opposition alliance says it will name sole presidential candidate for this year's general election.
- A woman alleged to have kidnapped six girls and taken them to a brothel in Nairobi is arrested.
- Attorney General Amos Wako pledges to conduct a thorough investigation into the death of Muruli.
- Nyanza Provincial Commissioner Joseph Kaguthi says politicians are transporting youth to create chaos at the Langata constituency by-election.
- A bomb scare stalls business at the headquarters of the Standard Chartered Bank of Kenya on Wednesday. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
